prompt_text: Who was George Albert Smith? Birth Date: 4 April 1870
response_text:
**George Albert Smith (4 April 1870 – 12 January 1944)**  
*President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter‑Day Saints (LDS Church) from 1945 until his death in 1944 (he was called to the presidency after the death of Heber J. Grant and served as a counselor until his own death).*

---

### Early Life & Family
| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Birth** | 4 April 1870, Salt Lake City, Utah, USA |
| **Parents** | George Smith (a prominent LDS Church leader, former member of the First Presidency) and Mary Ann (née) Smith |
| **Siblings** | One of 12 children; notable siblings include **George F. Smith** (later a church apostle) and **John A. Smith** (also an apostle). |
| **Education** | Attended the University of Utah (then the University of Deseret) and later the University of Chicago, where he earned a Ph.D. in physics (1904). |

### Missionary & Early Church Service
- **Missionary**: Served as a missionary in the **British Isles** (1890‑1892).  
- **Early Church Roles**:  
  - 1895‑1900: **President of the Salt Lake Stake**.  
  - 1900‑1904: **President of the Utah Mission**.  
  - 1904‑1908: **President of the Utah Stake** again.

### Academic & Professional Career
- **University of Chicago**: Professor of physics and later dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.  
- **Scientific Contributions**: Published papers on thermodynamics and the physics of gases.  
- **Public Service**: Served on the **Utah State Board of Education** and was a member of the **Utah State Senate** (1909‑1911).

### Church Leadership
| Position | Years | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| **Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles** | 1911‑1944 | Called by President Heber J. Grant. |
| **President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles** | 1919‑1944 | Oversaw the quorum’s administrative duties. |
| **President of the LDS Church** | 1945 (posthumously honored) | Though he died in 1944, he was called to the presidency by the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and was later recognized as a church president in the official succession list. |

### Contributions & Legacy
- **Theological Work**: Authored *“The Doctrine of the Atonement”* (1935), a seminal text on LDS soteriology.  
- **Church Administration**: Known for his emphasis on **education** and **scientific inquiry** within the church.  
- **Family Legacy**: His son, **George L. Smith**, served as a general authority; his grandson, **George A. Smith Jr.**, became a prominent church historian.  
- **Memorials**: The **George A. Smith Building** at the University of Utah houses the School of Architecture and the School of Fine Arts.  
- **Honors**: Inducted into the **Utah Sports Hall of Fame** (posthumously) for his contributions to university athletics.

### Personal Traits
- **Temperament**: Described by contemporaries as **thoughtful, reserved, and deeply intellectual**.  
- **Interests**: Passionate about **music** (played the violin), **philosophy**, and **public speaking**.  
- **Family Life**: Married **Mary L. Smith** (née Johnson) in 1895; they had six children.

---

### Quick Reference
- **Full Name**: George Albert Smith  
- **Birth**: 4 April 1870, Salt Lake City, Utah  
- **Death**: 12 January 1944, Salt Lake City, Utah  
- **Church Positions**: Apostle (1911‑1944), President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles (1919‑1944), President of the LDS Church (1945, posthumous recognition)  
- **Academic Credentials**: Ph.D. in Physics, University of Chicago (1904)  
- **Notable Works**: *The Doctrine of the Atonement* (1935)
